questions.note: Findability from type weight and spacing is a pixel question, deferred to the built finalist. Auditable intent: the board makes the page's purpose its own shape (rows are players, columns are what the repo can state), and hatched blanks give the unknown a visible form; the risk carried to the build is that a board's uniform cell weight offers no first-read entry point at 390.

questions.element: hatched blank cells (45-degree --rule stripes) and rules on both axes
questions.evidence: none - concept round, no build (discipline rule 10)
questions.note: Whether hatching reads as honesty or as texture noise is a surface-as-it-reads judgement and waits for pixels. The text-level signal: on day one most cells are empty by the packet's own admission, so the loudest mark on the flagship would be a repeated non-discriminating pattern - R8's forbidden shape in a new channel.

Judged only from the packet text plus RULES.md R7-R13 and JUDGE.md; no pixel property was scored and nothing below a fold was inferred. The R7 and R13 challenges were judged as arguments (discipline rule 11), not failed for being challenges.

findings.problem: On day one the board is mostly hatched blanks, so the most repeated mark on the flagship surface is a texture that discriminates nothing between rows.
findings.invariant: No cell treatment that is applied to a majority of cells carries more visual weight than the cells that hold a value.
findings.prescription: Render the empty cell as its text alternate at --muted with no pattern, and reserve the hatch for a column that is empty in full.

findings.problem: The home Frontier door is defined as three rows of a horizontally scrolling board with no stated column or height budget, on the one page the brief requires to lead with the changed feed.
findings.invariant: At 390 the home first viewport shows at least as many changed-feed items as the current capture, and the door does not introduce a horizontal scroll on the home page.
findings.prescription: Make the door a fixed two-column excerpt (player, newest listing) rather than a board fragment.

findings.problem: R8 classes are named only for the board surfaces; /tools, /data and the home changed feed are governed by R8's applied list today and the packet does not say whether the board's column tokens reach them.
findings.invariant: Every surface the board grid touches carries a stated R8 class justified against R8's test.
findings.prescription: State the class per surface in the packet before build, as the board explicitly spreads to /catalog and /wiki index.

findings.problem: A uniform ruled grid gives a first-time reader no ranked entry point: every cell is set at the same weight, so nothing declares where to start.
findings.invariant: One element on /frontier is set at a weight no other element on the surface uses, and it names the page's purpose.
findings.prescription: Give the board a single dominant column (the player name, or the newest listing) rather than an even tabulation.

diagnosis.strongest: DENS - the only packet that names R8's test and applies it, and the only one that puts /wiki/model/<entry> in scope so F-K12's second half is answerable; the catalog@390 two-line form matches R12's priority fields exactly.
diagnosis.weakest: HIER - a uniform tabulation is a shape without a first read, and the packet's own risks say most of it is empty on day one.
diagnosis.critical_issue: The flagship's dominant visual mark on day one would be the hatch, a repeated non-discriminating pattern, which is R8's forbidden shape relocated into texture.
diagnosis.highest_value_improvement: Demote the empty cell to muted text and promote one column to a dominant weight, so the board acquires a first-read entry point and the honest blank stops being the loudest thing on the page.

downstream.weakness: The concept's persuasive claim (honest blanks) and its hierarchy problem (nothing leads) are the same design decision.
downstream.cause: A board asserts that all cells matter equally; K10's amazement requirement asks for one thing that arrests a first-time reader.
downstream.recommendation: If built, capture /frontier at 390 first - the horizontal-scroll container is where the board's density claim either holds or collapses.
